Indian boxers produced a dominant display on Friday, with six of them entering the finals of their respective bouts to assure at least silver medals in Glasgow.First to make the final was Bhiwani’s Preeti Pawar , who defeated Zambia’s Catherine Mwape 5-0 in the women’s 54kg semifinals. In the men’s 80kg last-four bout, Ankush Panghal also had an easy outing against his Canadian opponent, Joshua Ofori, winning 5-0 to advance to the final. Jaismine Lamboria showed her aggression from the start, winning her women’s 57kg semifinal by referee stops contest (RSC) against Lesotho’s Rapelang Maselela. Arundhati Choudhary fought a spirited bout to beat defending champion Rosie Eccles of Wales 4-0 in the women’s 70kg semifinals.Arundhati, who became the first boxer from Rajasthan to compete at the CWG, looked in total control. She used her feet well, moved around the ring smartly and landed her punches regularly, keeping the experienced Welsh boxer under constant pressure to book her place in the gold-medal clash.Jadumani Singh, who had displayed excellent reflexes and quick punches in his earlier bouts, continued his fine form in the men’s 55kg semifinals against Namibia’s Philip Haoseb, securing a 5-0 victory.Although Philip had the height advantage, Jadumani used his defensive skills to duck the Namibian’s charges and land clean punches in return, convincing the judges of his superiority.In the women’s 51kg semifinal later in the evening, Sakshi Chaudhary defeated Canada’s Amber-Jane Wall 5-0 on points.In the track events, the Indian mixed 4x400m relay team qualified for the final after finishing seventh overall in the round-one heats on Friday. The Indian quartet of Vishal TK, Anisa Babu, Rajesh Ramesh and Rashdeep Kaur clocked 3:20.98 to finish fourth in Heat 2 and sneak into Saturday’s final.In the field, Tajinderpal Singh Toor and Samardeep Singh Gill finished fifth and seventh respectively in the men’s shot put final on Thursday. National record holder Animesh Kujur finished sixth in his men’s 200m heat in 20.65 seconds. Kujur had set a national record of 20.32s at the Asian Championships last year.In the women’s 5000m, Parul Chaudhary finished 13th, clocking 15:08.56 to end her campaign outside the top 10.
Article Summary: Indian boxers produced a dominant display on Friday, with six of them entering the finals of their respective bouts to assure at least silver medals. First to make the final was Bhiwani's Preeti Pawar, who defeated Zambia’s Catherine Mwape 5-0 in the women's 54kg semifinals. Arundhati Choudhary fought a spirited bout to beat defending champion Rosie Eccles of Wales.

Article Title: Commonwealth Games 2026: Asmita Dey, Harsh Singh script historic judo double
Article Text:
Asmita Dey, Harsh Singh (Agency Image)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Indian judo at the Commonwealth Games had seemed destined to be associated with Tulika Mann’s withdrawal from participation after the 2022 Birmingham silver-winning judoka was suspended for a whereabouts failure.How things can change in a week.On Friday, riding on yukos and waza-aris of their own making, Asmita Dey, daughter of a cycle mechanic in Belonia, south Tripura, and Delhi’s Harsh Singh changed the narrative and created history by winning gold medals in the women’s -48kg and men’s -60kg finals respectively. The third finalist, Yamini Mourya, from Sagar in Madhya Pradesh, however, had to settle for silver after losing by ippon to England’s Acelya Toprak in the women’s -57kg summit clash.Asmita and Harsh added to India’s gold medals in Glasgow, which have so far come through Mirabai Chanu (women’s 48kg weightlifting), Sharmila Dhankar (women’s shot put F57), and Dilip Gavit (men’s 100m T47).In her final, the 23-year-old Asmita fought off a spirited challenge from Canada’s Heidi Quach to prevail by yuko (2-1) in a composed and determined display. Asmita initially conceded a point and then received a penalty, giving Quach a 1-0 lead and control of the bout.But the Indian fought her way back into the game with a strong attack to level the scores at 1-1. After the scores were levelled, both Asmita and Quach failed to score further in the four minutes of regulation time, and the match headed towards the Golden Score period, where the first scoring action determines the winner.Asmita did just what the doctors had prescribed. She didn’t waste any time and launched a series of attacks on her opponent to earn a yuko, awarded when the judoka throws the opponent to the floor or pins them for 5-6 seconds.“I have worked so hard for this. Before this medal, I was unable to sleep. I used to stay awake thinking about the fights. Even if my body was tired, I was not able to sleep. I used to feel restless and then wake up for training at 5:30 am,” Asmita was quoted as saying by PTI.An 800m runner as a kid, Asmita’s victory brought much-deserved cheers to the Indian camp and made Harsh, the next finalist, even more confident ahead of his title bout against Australia’s Olympian Joshua Katz.Delhi’s Harsh, participating in his maiden CWG, didn’t let his inexperience come between him and the gold. The 23-year-old may not have been able to score initially, but he didn’t allow Katz to get away either. He held his ground and waited for the right opportunity, which came with just 40 seconds left in regulation time.Harsh executed a waza-ari by throwing Katz onto his side and held him for a few seconds before the Australian got back to his feet. Harsh remained calm and didn’t allow Katz to counterattack in the final few seconds of regulation time.
Article Summary: Asmita Dey and Harsh Singh win gold medals in women's -48kg and men's -60kg finals respectively. Yamini Mourya, from Sagar in Madhya Pradesh, had to settle for silver after losing by ippon to England’s Acelya Toprak in the women�'s -57kg summit clash.

Article Title: How Yashvir Singh's self-talk inspired a historic javelin bronze at Commonwealth Games
Article Text:
Yashvir Singh (Image credit: X)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Yashvir Singh had one thought in his mind before stepping up for his final throw at Scotstoun Stadium. The bronze medal mark was just beyond 82 metres, and he reminded himself that he had already crossed that distance before.With that belief, the 24-year-old gave everything on his sixth and final attempt. His javelin landed at 85.41m, setting a new personal best, earning him a historic bronze medal and helping India complete a memorable double on the podium alongside Neeraj Chopra at the Commonwealth Games 2026.The Commonwealth Games debutant improved his previous personal best of 83.72m when it mattered the most."This is my first international medal, and I am overjoyed. Everyone supported me, my family, my parents, everyone... I am truly happy about this... things were going a bit sluggishly at the start. At one point, my throw was around 81.3 meters. I saw that the bronze medal mark was sitting at 82 meters. I told myself, 'I've already thrown 82 meters--my personal best--in this competition, so I can definitely go beyond that. ' Things weren't going well up to the fifth throw, so for the final attempt, I decided to just go for it and see what happens.That last throw turned out really well," Yashvir said after winning the medal.Competing in only his second event of the season, Olympic champion Neeraj Chopra registered a season-best throw of 85.83m in his second attempt to win the silver medal despite the cold and windy conditions.Sri Lanka's Rumesh Tharanga Pathirage claimed the gold with a brilliant throw of 89.75m.Neeraj later said sharing the podium with Yashvir made the achievement even more special."It brings back memories of the Asian Games, where Saurav and I both won medals. I'm really happy that Yashvir achieved a personal best at such a crucial moment. It feels great to be on the podium together. It's always a joy to hear the national anthem play. That said, I also achieved a season-best, and my comeback is progressing well. There are more competitions ahead, so I'm very happy," Chopra told reporters.
Article Summary: Yashvir Singh wins historic bronze medal at Commonwealth Games 2026. The 24-year-old's throw of 85.41m was a new personal best. Olympic champion Neeraj Chopra claimed the silver medal. Sri Lanka's Rumesh Tharanga Pathirage claimed the gold with a throw of 89.75m.

Article Title: CWG 2026: India’s finest day in Glasgow yet! Six medals, 10 boxing finalists and 23-medal tally secured
Article Text:
India’s biggest day at CWG 2026 sees six medals won, 10 boxers reach finals and the tally rise to 23.

Judo delivers historic double gold

Athletics adds three more medals



Perfect day for Indian boxing





Narender Berwal defeated Nigel Paul of Trinidad and Tobago to reach the men's 90kg+ final.

Sachin Siwach beat Wales' Owain Harris-Allan to qualify for the men's 60kg final.

Lovlina Borgohain overcame Tarona Khanum Badi Pasoni Taafaki of Tuvalu to reach the women's 75kg final.

Priya Ghanghas defeated England's Lucy Kings-Wheatley to book her place in the women's 60kg final.

Sakshi Choudhary beat Canada's Amber-Jane Wall to advance to the women's 51kg final.

Jadumani Singh defeated Namibia's Philip Haoseb to qualify for the men's 55kg final.

Arundhati Choudhary overcame Wales' Rosie Eccles to reach the women's 70kg final.

Jaismine Lamboria defeated Lesotho's Rapelang Maselela to progress to the women's 57kg final.

Ankush Panghal beat Canada's Joshua Ofori to secure a place in the men's 80kg final.

Preeti Pawar defeated Zambia's Catherine Mwape to qualify for the women's 54kg final.

Bowls and cycling campaign continues





Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Another major step forward



India enjoyed one of their finest days of the 2026 Commonwealth Games on Friday, collecting six medals across judo and athletics while also producing a flawless performance inside the boxing ring, where all 10 Indian semi-finalists booked their places in Saturday's gold medal bouts.By the end of Day 9, India had increased its overall medal tally to 23 medals- five gold, 12 silver and six bronze, remaining 10th in the standings, just one medal behind ninth-placed Wales.The medals came from two sports, but India's success stretched far beyond the podium, with athletes progressing to finals, securing qualification places and keeping several medal hopes alive heading into the closing stages of the Games.India's day began on the judo mat with a historic breakthrough.Asmita Dey claimed gold in the women's 48kg event after defeating Canada's Heidi Quach 2-1 in a dramatic final. After recovering from an early setback, Asmita forced the contest into Golden Score before producing the decisive Yuko to become one of India's Commonwealth champions.Soon afterwards, Harsh Singh created history by becoming the first Indian male judoka to win a Commonwealth Games gold medal.He defeated Australia's Joshua Katz 10-0 (Waza-Ari) in the men's 60kg final after controlling the contest before producing the match-winning throw late in the bout.India completed a memorable day in judo when Yamini Mourya secured silver in the women's 57kg category. She pushed England's Acelya Toprak through a tightly contested final that extended into Golden Score before eventually settling for silver after receiving a third Shido penalty.Not every Indian judoka advanced. Shraddha Kopade bowed out after losing to Wales' Lola Hodson in the women's 52kg repechage, while Rohit Majgul exited the men's 66kg competition following defeat to England's Michael Fryer in the repechage.Indian athletics added another three medals before producing several encouraging performances elsewhere.Tejaswin Shankar became the first Indian athlete to win a Commonwealth Games decathlon medal, collecting bronze with 7,976 points. His effort placed him behind Grenada's Lindon Victor (8,096) and Canada's Damian Warner (8,036), adding another historic achievement to his Birmingham 2022 high jump bronze.The men's javelin final then produced a double podium for India.Neeraj Chopra won silver with a season-best throw of 85.83m, finishing behind Sri Lanka's Rumesh Tharanga Pathirage, who claimed gold with 89.75m.Alongside him on the podium stood Yash Vir Singh, whose personal-best 85.41m secured bronze after a superb late improvement during the competition.Elsewhere on the track, India's mixed 4x400m relay quartet of Vishal TK, Rajesh Ramesh, Rashdeep Kaur and Neeru Pathak safely negotiated the heats to qualify for the final.In the men's 400m hurdles, Yashas Palaksha and Santhosh Kumar Thamilarasan finished seventh and eighth respectively, missing out on the medals.If judo produced history, boxing produced perfection.Every one of India's 10 semi-finalists won their bouts to reach the finals, guaranteeing themselves at least silver medals while remaining in contention for gold.The finalists are:The clean sweep means all 10 Indian finalists will now compete for Commonwealth Games gold on Saturday.India also remained active in bowls.The men's pairs combination of Dinesh Kumar(1) and Navneet Singh defeated the Falkland Islands in sectional play to continue their campaign, while Nayanmoni Saikia recorded a victory over Zambia's Mildred Mkandawire in the women's singles competition.Track cycling, however, proved more difficult.Dinesh Kumar(2) and Harshveer Singh were eliminated from the men's 4,000m individual pursuit, while Ronaldo Singh, David Beckham Elkatohchoongo, and Jemsh Singh all exited in their respective heats of the men's keirin competition.Friday combined immediate success with encouraging progress for the days ahead.India produced its biggest medal haul of the Games so far, celebrated historic achievements in judo and athletics, registered a memorable double podium in the men's javelin, and watched every one of its 10 boxers advance into gold medal bouts.With 23 medals already secured and a host of finals still to come, India's strongest phase of the Glasgow Commonwealth Games campaign could still lie ahead.
Article Summary: India enjoyed one of their finest days of the 2026 Commonwealth Games on Friday, collecting six medals across judo and athletics. All 10 Indian semi-finalists booked their places in Saturday's gold medal bouts. India had increased its overall medal tally to 23 medals- five gold, 12 silver and six bronze.

Article Title: Dream debut! FC Raengdai stun Indian Navy to make Durand Cup history
Article Text:
FC Raengdai players after their goal in Imphal on Thursday/ Credit: Durand Cup Media

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

On Thursday, the oldest football tournament in Asia saw its newest competitors script a memorable win on debut at the Khuman Lampak Stadium in Imphal.FC Raengdai, the third Manipur club at the 135th edition of the Durand Cup, defeated last year’s quarterfinalists, Indian Navy Football Team, with a solitary goal in their Group D fixture and making a winning start to their campaign.Founded in 2022 by a group of football enthusiasts from Zeliangrongpui community, Raengdei announced their arrival in the historic tournament – in front of fans in the Manipur capital – when super-sub Khaidem Amarjit Singh kicked in the decisive goal in the 58th minute of the game.“Football is as much about belief as it is about ability. Today, the difference was the faith this team had in each other,” Raengdai coach Kshetrimayum Birbal Singh told TOI after the win.“The boys trusted the work they’ve put in, they stayed together through every moment of the game and they never lost belief. That’s why we came away with the result and I’m very proud of every single one of them.While both teams had their chances in the match, it was only in the second half that saw a double substitution from the coach – introducing Laishram Bikramjit Singh and Amarjit — that the debutants got the breakthrough.Novin Gurung, the last man in defence for Indian Navy, was dispossessed by Mridul Doley, who drove into the penalty area. Although the advancing goalkeeper brought Doley down, the loose ball rolled kindly into the path of substitute Amarjit, who completed the simplest of tap-ins into an empty net to seal a 1-0 victory and score Raengdai's first-ever goal in the Durand Cup.
Article Summary: FC Raengdai defeated Indian Navy Football Team 1-0 in the Durand Cup on Thursday. Khaidem Amarjit Singh scored the decisive goal in the 58th minute of the game. Raengdei are the third Manipur club at the 135th edition of the tournament.

Article Title: ‘I fell asleep’: World Cup-snubbed Cole Palmer admits missing half of England’s win over Mexico
Article Text:
Chelsea's Cole Palmer stands on the pitch during the English Premier League soccer match between Manchester City and Chelsea in Manchester, England, Sunday, Jan. 4, 2026. (AP Photo/Dave Thompson)

Palmer admits he missed half of England's biggest World Cup win

England produced one of their finest World Cup victories

World Cup omission continues to motivate Palmer

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Ready for a fresh start under Xabi Alonso

Cole Palmer has revealed that he accidentally slept through part of England's dramatic World Cup round-of-16 victory over Mexico after staying up to watch the match from Australia during Chelsea's pre-season tour.The Chelsea midfielder, who was surprisingly left out of Thomas Tuchel's 26-man squad for the 2026 FIFA World Cup , admitted he nodded off at half-time during England's eventual 3-2 victory at the Estadio Azteca, one of the standout matches of the tournament.Palmer made the light-hearted admission while speaking to reporters during Chelsea's pre-season preparations, drawing laughter from those present.Asked whether he had followed England's World Cup campaign, Palmer said he had watched the knockout tie against Mexico, although the late kick-off proved too much."Watching World Cup? Yeah; I watched Mexico vs England but fell asleep at half time."Speaking further about following the tournament from Australia, Palmer explained that the unusual match timings made it difficult to watch every game live."Obviously I was away, and the times were a bit crazy in America, so it was a bit difficult, but I did watch the games."The round-of-16 fixture kicked off in the early hours of the morning after severe weather delayed the start by an hour, making it a challenging watch for viewers in different time zones.Palmer may have missed the second half, but England went on to produce one of their most memorable World Cup performances.Jude Bellingham struck twice before half-time to give England control of the contest, before Mexico mounted a comeback after the break.England were then reduced to 10 men following Jarell Quansah's red card but held firm, with Harry Kane converting a decisive penalty as Tuchel's side secured a hard-fought 3-2 victory at the Azteca Stadium to reach the quarter-finals.The result was widely regarded as one of England's finest victories away from home in World Cup history.Palmer was one of the biggest names left out of England's squad despite enjoying another impressive campaign with Chelsea.Reflecting on the disappointment, the 24-year-old admitted being overlooked has become a source of motivation ahead of the new season."Naturally, if someone tells you that you're not good enough to join the squad, you'll put in extra effort."Although missing the World Cup was a major setback, Palmer acknowledged there was one positive after an injury-disrupted 2025-26 campaign, as it finally allowed him to recover physically.He also shared another typically understated anecdote while discussing treatment for his long-standing groin problem."I went to Denmark, Sweden, one of those countries can't remember to discuss surgery, but we decided I didn't need to get it."After seeking specialist medical advice in Scandinavia, Palmer ultimately avoided surgery and has returned fully fit for Chelsea's preparations.Palmer is now focused on the upcoming campaign under new Chelsea head coach Xabi Alonso, with the midfielder fully involved in the club's pre-season programme.Chelsea continue their preparations with a friendly against Tottenham Hotspur before opening their Premier League campaign against Fulham later in August.Having used the summer to recover after an injury-hit season and the disappointment of missing England's World Cup squad, Palmer will now look to force his way back into Thomas Tuchel's plans with strong performances at club level.
Article Summary: Cole Palmer admits he accidentally slept through part of England's World Cup round-of-16 victory over Mexico. The Chelsea midfielder stayed up to watch the match from Australia during Chelsea's pre-season tour. The 24-year-old was surprisingly left out of Thomas Tuchel's 26-man squad for the 2026 FIFA World Cup.

Article Title: ISL: Jamshedpur FC pull out of 2026-27 season; Inter Kashi pay Rs 55 lakh participation fees
Article Text:
Jamshedpur FC have withdrawn from the 2026–27 ISL season but will continue investing in grassroots football development.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Inter Kashi pay participation fee



New Delhi: Jamshedpur FC , the 2022 Indian Super League Shield winners, have decided not to play the 2026-27 season of India's top-tier football competition. The club, owned and managed by Tata Steel , had not paid its Rs 55 lakh participation fees towards the upcoming club-led model. With an extension granted until July 31, the 2025 Super Cup runners-up decided to cease operations rather than pay the fees.“Jamshedpur Football Club would like to confirm that it will not be participating in ISL from the 2026-27 season onwards,” the club said in an official statement.“JFSPL (Jamshedpur Football and Sporting Private Limited) remains committed, in other capacities, to the continued growth and development of football in India. We will continue in our endeavour to promote and develop the game of football, including at the grassroots level.”TimesofIndia.com has learnt that the decision not to participate in the 2026-27 ISL season is not a snap judgement. The club had been mulling its options even before a deal was reached between the AIFF and the clubs earlier in the month over the league's roadmap.Additionally, the parent group and the club will honour their commitments towards players, coaches and support staff who have long-running contracts.Jamshedpur FC, founded in 2017 and playing their first ISL season in 2017-18, will continue to work in grassroots development, with the Tata Football Academy based in Jamshedpur central to those plans.“We will continue to identify and develop young football talent across India to create a strong pathway for young players from grassroots to national and international football,” the club continued in their statement.In their brief stay in Indian men's club football, Jamshedpur FC clinched the League Winners’ Shield under Owen Coyle in 2021-22. They then reached the last-four of the ISL Cup and the AIFF Super Cup final in the 2024-25 season under Khalid Jamil.Besides Jamshedpur FC, Inter Kashi was the other ISL club that had not paid its Rs 55 lakh participation fees by July 20 and was given an extension until July 31. On Friday, the club paid a substantial chunk of that amount despite the challenging financial position they find themselves in. The club was also hit with a transfer ban until the end of 2027 after failing to pay outstanding wages to players and coaching staff.While paying a big portion of their participation fees towards the 2026-27 ISL season, Inter Kashi have also asked the AIFF to waive the Rs 1 lakh per day fine. They and Jamshedpur FC were both handed punishments for not paying the participation fees by the July 20 deadline.
Article Summary: Jamshedpur FC have withdrawn from the 2026-27 ISL season. The club had not paid its Rs 55 lakh participation fees towards the upcoming club-led model. The 2025 Super Cup runners-up decided to cease operations rather than pay the fees.

Article Title: Why Spain and Portugal could miss 2030 World Cup they are set to host if FIFA and UEFA fail to reach agreement
Article Text:
Spain and Portugal could face missing their own 2030 World Cup as FIFA-UEFA battle escalates.

UEFA's boycott threat carries major implications

FILE - UEFA President Aleksander Ceferin, left, talks to FIFA President Gianni Infantino before a round of sixteen match between Switzerland and Italy at the Euro 2024 soccer tournament in Berlin, Germany, Saturday, June 29, 2024. (AP Photo/Matthias Schrader, File)

Why Spain and Portugal are at the centre of the debate

Morocco's position remains unclear

Expansion plans add another layer of uncertainty

Also read:

FIFA insists consultation remains open

Pressure continues to build on Infantino

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The escalating dispute between FIFA and UEFA over Gianni Infantino's controversial World Cup investment proposal is no longer just a governance battle. If FIFA presses ahead with the plan and UEFA follows through on its boycott threat, an unprecedented scenario could unfold at the 2030 World Cup, with co-hosts Spain and Portugal potentially absent from the tournament they are due to stage.The prospect has emerged after UEFA unanimously declared that none of its national teams would participate in FIFA competitions "for so long as these proposals remain alive", while FIFA has insisted it will continue consulting its 211 member associations on plans to establish FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), a new commercial subsidiary that would sell a minority stake in the governing body's commercial rights to private investors.Although no decision has yet been taken and FIFA maintains that the proposal can still be approved, amended or rejected, the standoff has raised fresh questions about what the 2030 World Cup could look like if neither side backs down.UEFA's warning followed an emergency meeting of its 55 member associations, which unanimously rejected FIFA's proposal."The World Cup cannot be treated as an investment product," UEFA said in its statement."It is one of football's greatest sporting legacies. It has been built over generations by players, national teams and supporters across every continent. No part of it should ever be surrendered to private investors."The World Cup is not for sale."The confederation later confirmed that none of its national teams would take part in FIFA competitions while the proposal remained under consideration, extending the position to both the men's and women's World Cups.UEFA vice-president Laura McAllister described the proposal as "catastrophic" and accused FIFA of using "a form of blackmail financially" through the funding package being offered to member associations that support the initiative.The implications are particularly significant because the 2030 World Cup is scheduled to be hosted primarily by Spain, Portugal and Morocco.The tournament will also feature one centenary match each in Uruguay, Argentina and Paraguay to commemorate the 100th anniversary of the inaugural FIFA World Cup, making it the first edition to span multiple continents in this way.If UEFA ultimately honours its boycott and Spain and Portugal remain bound by the confederation's position, the two European co-hosts would not participate in the tournament despite hosting the majority of the competition.Such a situation would be unprecedented in World Cup history, with principal host nations absent not because they failed to qualify, but because of a dispute between football's governing bodies.Unlike UEFA, Concacaf and the Asian Football Confederation (AFC), the Confederation of African Football (CAF) has not formally declared its position on FIFA's investment proposal.CAF initially indicated it was open to the consultation process, while Morocco, one of the three principal hosts for 2030, has not publicly stated whether it supports or opposes the creation of FIFA Forward Enterprise.South America's governing body, CONMEBOL, has likewise not taken an official position on the investment proposal. However, its president, Alejandro Domínguez, has previously backed expanding the 2030 World Cup to 64 teams.That leaves the positions of two of the six host nations and their confederations unresolved as FIFA's consultation process continues.The political uncertainty comes as FIFA has simultaneously accelerated work on a possible expansion of the 2030 World Cup from 48 to 64 teams.Internal documents seen by multiple media outlets show FIFA has begun seeking an independent assessment of the sporting, commercial and operational consequences of a larger tournament, with the governing body expecting the study to be completed before member associations vote on the FFE proposal in September.If both developments were ultimately approved, the World Cup would expand to 64 teams just one edition after increasing from 32 to 48 teams in 2026.The combination of a significantly larger tournament and the possible absence of UEFA nations would fundamentally reshape the competition. Spain and Portugal would not only lose the opportunity to compete on home soil, but FIFA would also face the prospect of staging its centenary World Cup without many of the sport's most successful national teams.While CONMEBOL has backed further expansion, others have expressed reservations. AFC president Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa has previously warned that another increase could create "chaos", while Concacaf president Victor Montagliani has questioned whether such a move would benefit the wider football ecosystem.Despite the growing backlash, FIFA has shown no sign of abandoning the proposal.Responding to criticism on Friday, the governing body insisted that "nobody is selling football" and rejected suggestions that the World Cup was being privatised.FIFA said FIFA Forward Enterprise had been proposed to allow member associations to benefit from football's commercial opportunities while preserving the governance of the game, adding that "everyone has the right to express their opposition" but that "no single entity can claim to represent all 211 Member Associations around the world."The organisation also stressed that the proposal remains part of an ongoing consultation process and that member associations retain the power to approve, amend or reject it. It added that if a majority does not support the plan, FIFA's commercial operations will remain unchanged and FIFA Forward Enterprise will not be established.The dispute has intensified rapidly over recent days.Concacaf rejected the proposal shortly after UEFA, while the AFC became the third confederation to oppose it, saying confidence in FIFA's governance had been "undermined".FIFA has also suffered an internal blow after senior adviser Carlos Cordeiro resigned with immediate effect, saying he opposed the proposal "unequivocally" and describing it as "a bad deal for football".With more than 100 national associations now represented by confederations that have publicly rejected the proposal, the debate has evolved far beyond a commercial restructuring plan. If FIFA proceeds and UEFA follows through on its threat, the consequences would extend beyond governance, potentially reshaping the composition of the 2030 World Cup and leaving Spain and Portugal absent from the very tournament they are due to co-host.
Article Summary: Spain and Portugal could miss their own 2030 World Cup as FIFA-UEFA battle escalates. Dispute over Gianni Infantino's controversial World Cup investment proposal is no longer just a governance battle. UEFA declared that none of its national teams would participate in FIFA competitions "for so long as these proposals remain alive"
